prompt.context_jp: 夜の街に、昼間の熱気___まだ少し残っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 夜の街に、昼間の熱気___まだ少し残っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this scene-setting line about the night streets.

feedback.correct_en: This sentence introduces the lingering daytime heat as new, observed information in the opening scene — a classic が use for presenting what exists in the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 熱気 a known topic being commented on, but it's just appearing in the narration. を would require a transitive verb, not 残る.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋に明かりがついている。
contrast_examples.en: There's a light on in the room. (new observation)

contrast_examples.jp: この部屋は暗い。
contrast_examples.en: This room is dark. (topic + comment)

prompt.context_jp: 由美___すぐには立ち去ろうとせず、舞の顔をじっと見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 由美___すぐには立ち去ろうとせず、舞の顔をじっと見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Yumi has already been introduced. Pick the particle that marks her as the ongoing topic.

feedback.correct_en: Yumi is the established topic the narrator keeps describing. は signals 'as for Yumi' and lets two linked actions (not leaving / staring) attach to her.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reintroduce her as new information, which clashes with her just being named. に would mark a destination/recipient.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は立ち去らず、じっと見つめていた。
contrast_examples.en: He didn't leave; he kept staring. (topic)

contrast_examples.jp: そこに彼が立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: He was standing there. (new presence)

prompt.context_jp: ふだんは 何があっても 動じない相馬さん___ すごく悩んでて…
prompt.prompt_jp: ふだんは 何があっても 動じない相馬さん___ すごく悩んでて…
prompt.prompt_en: Mai is reporting a surprising new state about Souma. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Mai is delivering news — the normally unshakeable Souma is suffering — as a fresh observation. が spotlights that unexpected subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame it as a general comment on Souma, losing the 'look at this surprising thing' feel. で doesn't fit the clause structure.

contrast_examples.jp: いつも冷静な彼が泣いていた。
contrast_examples.en: He, who's always calm, was crying. (striking new info)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼はいつも冷静だ。
contrast_examples.en: He is always calm. (general topic comment)

prompt.context_jp: 2人はホントに いい関係だったわ タイプ___全然 違うんだけど とても気が合って…
prompt.prompt_jp: タイプ___全然 違うんだけど とても気が合って…
prompt.prompt_en: Yumi contrasts their differing types against their good chemistry. Which particle carries the contrast?

feedback.correct_en: は sets up a contrastive frame: 'as for their types, totally different — BUT they got along.' The けど depends on this contrastive setup.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just report 'their types differ' as neutral new info, losing the explicit 'but' pivot that follows. を doesn't fit 違う.

contrast_examples.jp: 顔は似てないけど、声はそっくり。
contrast_examples.en: Faces aren't alike, but voices are identical. (contrast)

contrast_examples.jp: 二人の顔が似ている。
contrast_examples.en: Their faces resemble each other. (plain statement)

prompt.context_jp: 私と相馬が結婚するって 決まったときも、いちばん喜んでくれたの___ 青井君だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: いちばん喜んでくれたの___ 青井君だった。
prompt.prompt_en: This is a cleft identifying who, out of everyone, was happiest. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: In the cleft 〜のは Xだった, は marks the presupposed set-up ('the one who was happiest') and Xだった identifies Aoi exhaustively as the answer.
feedback.incorrect_en: が on のは is ungrammatical here. も would mean 'also,' which doesn't fit a single identification.

contrast_examples.jp: 最初に来たのは田中さんだ。
contrast_examples.en: The one who came first was Tanaka. (cleft identification)

contrast_examples.jp: 最初に田中さんが来た。
contrast_examples.en: Tanaka came first. (plain subject)

prompt.context_jp: 相馬のそばにいながら、自分___何ひとつできなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 相馬のそばにいながら、自分___何ひとつできなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Mai contrasts her closeness to Souma with her helplessness. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: は highlights 自分 against an implied contrast ('others might have helped, but as for me...'). This matches the regretful 〜ながら setup.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just neutrally identify the subject and lose the self-reproach. に doesn't suit できなかった here.

contrast_examples.jp: 他の人はできた。私はできなかった。
contrast_examples.en: Others could. I couldn't. (contrast)

contrast_examples.jp: 私ができなかった。
contrast_examples.en: It was I who couldn't. (identifies the agent)

prompt.context_jp: 私も何もできなかったなぁ… 相馬___ いちばんつらいときに
prompt.prompt_jp: 相馬___ いちばんつらいときに
prompt.prompt_en: Inside a 〜ときに relative clause describing when Souma was suffering. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a subordinate 〜とき clause, the subject takes が. The clause specifies 'the time when Souma was suffering' — pure identification of the subject within that clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は normally reaches out to the main clause as a topic; it feels wrong trapped inside a 〜とき relative. を would need a transitive verb.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来たとき、私は寝ていた。
contrast_examples.en: When he came, I was sleeping. (が in sub-clause)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は来たとき、疲れていた。
contrast_examples.en: He, when he came, was tired. (topic over whole sentence)

prompt.context_jp: そこには、息を切らした舞___立っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: そこには、息を切らした舞___立っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Souma turns around and discovers Mai standing there. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: This is a classic 'there appeared/was X' discovery sentence. が presents Mai as the surprising new entity in the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly treat Mai as the ongoing topic being commented on. で is used for means or location of action, not existence.

contrast_examples.jp: そこに知らない人が立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: A stranger was standing there. (presentation)

contrast_examples.jp: 舞はそこに立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: Mai was standing there. (comment on known Mai)

prompt.context_jp: 舞は、相馬の拳___膝の上で固く握られているのに気づいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 相馬の拳___膝の上で固く握られているのに気づいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Mai notices Souma's fist clenched. Which particle marks the thing noticed?

feedback.correct_en: Inside the embedded 気づく clause, 相馬の拳 is new information Mai perceives. が marks subjects of such 〜のに気づく complements.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly promote the fist to the main-clause topic across 気づいた. を doesn't fit the passive 握られている.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が泣いているのに気づいた。
contrast_examples.en: I noticed that he was crying.

contrast_examples.jp: ドアが開いているのに気づいた。
contrast_examples.en: I noticed that the door was open.

prompt.context_jp: でもな… 俺___ お前の友達だろう
prompt.prompt_jp: 俺___ お前の友達だろう
prompt.prompt_en: Souma pleads with Aoi, stating his role. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: Souma asserts 'as for me, I'm your friend, right?' — a topic-comment declaration about himself. は is the natural choice.
feedback.incorrect_en: 俺が お前の友達だろう would sound like 'I'M your friend (not someone else)' — exhaustive identification, which doesn't match the emotional appeal here.

contrast_examples.jp: 俺はお前の味方だ。
contrast_examples.en: I'm on your side. (topic-comment)

contrast_examples.jp: 俺がお前の味方だ。
contrast_examples.en: I'M the one on your side. (exclusive identification)

prompt.context_jp: 相馬さんは あなた___ 友達だから 苦しんでるんです！
prompt.prompt_jp: 相馬さんは あなた___ 友達だから 苦しんでるんです！
prompt.prompt_en: Inside the だから subordinate clause 'because you are a friend.' Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: 相馬さんは is already the main-clause topic. Inside the embedded だから clause, 'you are a friend' takes が for its subject — one は per sentence, roughly.
feedback.incorrect_en: Using は again on あなた would compete with 相馬さんは for topic status and sound off. を doesn't fit the copular 友達だ.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は君が来るから喜んでいる。
contrast_examples.en: He's happy because you're coming.

contrast_examples.jp: 君は来るから、彼は喜んでいる。
contrast_examples.en: You're coming, so he's happy. (two independent topics)

prompt.context_jp: 相馬の顔から、静かに血の気___引いていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 相馬の顔から、静かに血の気___引いていった。
prompt.prompt_en: Souma learns the shocking truth. Which particle marks the 'blood' draining?

feedback.correct_en: 血の気が引く is a fixed collocation describing an involuntary bodily event — pure new information in the narration. が is standard.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame 血の気 as a topic being discussed, which is unnatural for this spontaneous physical change. を doesn't fit intransitive 引く here.

contrast_examples.jp: 顔から血の気が引いた。
contrast_examples.en: The color drained from his face.

contrast_examples.jp: 涙が出た。
contrast_examples.en: Tears came out. (spontaneous event)

prompt.context_jp: 家族___いると どんなことをしても 守ってやらなきゃならないからな
prompt.prompt_jp: 家族___いると どんなことをしても 守ってやらなきゃならないからな
prompt.prompt_en: Souma reflects on having a family. Which particle fits with いる in this 〜と conditional?

feedback.correct_en: 家族がいる 'to have family' is an existence predicate, and the thing that exists takes が. Inside the conditional 〜と clause, が is especially natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: 家族は would turn 'family' into a topic, suggesting contrast ('as for family…'), which sounds odd for a general conditional. を doesn't go with いる.

contrast_examples.jp: お金があると安心する。
contrast_examples.en: When you have money, you feel at ease.

contrast_examples.jp: お金はあるけど、時間がない。
contrast_examples.en: I have money, but no time. (contrastive は)

prompt.context_jp: 女___ 守るものができると 強くなるけど 男___ 守るものができると 逆に 弱くなる
prompt.prompt_jp: 女___ 守るものができると 強くなるけど 男___ 守るものができると 逆に 弱くなる
prompt.prompt_en: Matsuki contrasts how women and men respond to having something to protect. Which particle fills both blanks?

feedback.correct_en: Both 女 and 男 are set up as contrasted frames: 'as for women… / as for men…'. The explicit けど…逆に signals the classic contrastive-は pattern on both sides.
feedback.incorrect_en: が/が would just report two neutral facts and lose the structured contrast. Mixing が/は breaks the parallel.

contrast_examples.jp: 夏は暑いけど、冬は寒い。
contrast_examples.en: Summer is hot but winter is cold. (parallel contrast)

contrast_examples.jp: 夏が暑い。
contrast_examples.en: Summer is (the one that is) hot. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: ようやく肩の荷が下りたせいか、皆の表情___穏やかだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 皆の表情___穏やかだった。
prompt.prompt_en: A general description of the group's mood after the ordeal. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: The narration zooms out and comments on everyone's expression as a whole. は fits the 'topic + descriptive comment' structure in a settled, summarizing sentence.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present 皆の表情 as surprising new information, but it's just the narrator stepping back to summarize the mood.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の顔は明るかった。
contrast_examples.en: His face was bright. (descriptive comment)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の顔が急に明るくなった。
contrast_examples.en: His face suddenly brightened. (noticed change)

prompt.context_jp: 相馬の顔には、驚きと苛立ちが入り混じった色___浮かんだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 相馬の顔には、驚きと苛立ちが入り混じった色___浮かんだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Narration describing an expression appearing on Souma's face. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: 顔に〜色が浮かぶ is a presentational expression: a new look appears. が spotlights the newly surfacing emotion.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly turn 色 into a topic being commented on. を doesn't fit the intransitive 浮かぶ.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の目に涙が浮かんだ。
contrast_examples.en: Tears welled up in his eyes.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女の顔に笑みが広がった。
contrast_examples.en: A smile spread across her face.

prompt.context_jp: 舞は差し出されたものを両手で受け取り、丁寧に頭を___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 舞は差し出されたものを両手で受け取り、丁寧に頭を___。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb completes this polite bowing gesture?

feedback.correct_en: 頭を下げる is the fixed collocation for bowing in Japanese — the only natural choice for a respectful gesture.
feedback.incorrect_en: 頭を落とす literally means 'drop one's head' and sounds grim/violent. 頭を振る means to shake one's head (no).

contrast_examples.jp: 深く頭を下げる。
contrast_examples.en: Bow deeply.

contrast_examples.jp: 首を振る。
contrast_examples.en: Shake one's head (to say no).

prompt.context_jp: 舞は由美に気を使いながら、言葉を___口を開いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 舞は由美に気を使いながら、言葉を___口を開いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Mai carefully picks what to say. Which verb fits '言葉を___'?

feedback.correct_en: 言葉を選ぶ 'to choose one's words' is a set collocation for speaking tactfully — exactly what Mai is doing with Yumi.
feedback.incorrect_en: 言葉を決める would mean 'decide on words' and isn't idiomatic. 言葉を集める would be 'collect words,' unrelated.

contrast_examples.jp: 慎重に言葉を選ぶ。
contrast_examples.en: Carefully choose one's words.

contrast_examples.jp: 一言一言、言葉を選んで話す。
contrast_examples.en: Speak choosing each word carefully.

prompt.context_jp: 腹___ 本音で話せる相手が なかなか いないってことも
prompt.prompt_jp: 腹___ 本音で話せる相手が なかなか いないってことも
prompt.prompt_en: Souma empathizes that lonely managers lack people they can really open up to. Fill the idiom.

feedback.correct_en: 腹を割って話す 'to speak with an open belly' means to speak frankly, holding nothing back — a well-known idiom.
feedback.incorrect_en: 腹を開ける/切る aren't idiomatic for 'speak frankly' (腹を切る literally evokes seppuku).

contrast_examples.jp: 一度、腹を割って話し合おう。
contrast_examples.en: Let's have a frank, open talk.

contrast_examples.jp: 本音をぶつける。
contrast_examples.en: Throw out one's true feelings.

prompt.context_jp: やがて青井の肩から、ふっと力が___。
prompt.prompt_jp: やがて青井の肩から、ふっと力が___。
prompt.prompt_en: Aoi's resistance crumbles. Which verb describes tension leaving the shoulders?

feedback.correct_en: 肩から力が抜ける is the standard idiom for tension draining from the body as someone relaxes or gives in.
feedback.incorrect_en: 力が落ちる means 'strength declines' (ability-wise), not momentary relaxation. 力が消える isn't idiomatic for this physical moment.

contrast_examples.jp: ホッとして肩の力が抜けた。
contrast_examples.en: I relaxed and the tension left my shoulders.

contrast_examples.jp: 体力が落ちる。
contrast_examples.en: Physical strength declines.

prompt.context_jp: 友人を苦しめながら頭を下げ続ける青井の姿に、舞の中で何かが___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 舞の中で何かが___。
prompt.prompt_en: Mai can no longer hold back her outrage. Which verb fits?

feedback.correct_en: 何かが切れる (literally 'something snapped') is the idiomatic way to describe an inner limit breaking — exactly Mai's emotional moment here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 折れる would suggest giving up/breaking down (心が折れる). 消える 'disappeared' doesn't capture the sudden rupture.

contrast_examples.jp: 堪忍袋の緒が切れた。
contrast_examples.en: My patience snapped.

contrast_examples.jp: 心が折れる。
contrast_examples.en: To be mentally crushed / lose heart.

prompt.context_jp: ___ですが… 昔からの友達なら どうして相馬さんの気持ちが 分からないんですか？
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ですが… 昔からの友達なら どうして相馬さんの気持ちが 分からないんですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Mai politely but firmly pushes back against Aoi. Which set phrase opens a respectful counter?

feedback.correct_en: お言葉を返すようですが is a fixed polite preface meaning 'I hate to talk back, but…' — exactly the register Mai uses to challenge Aoi respectfully.
feedback.incorrect_en: お話を伺う means 'to listen humbly,' not to disagree. 言葉を交わす means 'exchange words' (casual chat), not pushback.

contrast_examples.jp: お言葉を返すようですが、それは違います。
contrast_examples.en: I hate to contradict you, but that's not right.

contrast_examples.jp: 失礼ですが、少し違うと思います。
contrast_examples.en: Excuse me, but I think that's a bit off.

prompt.context_jp: 善良な経営者の弱みに___、友人を欺くことまで強要して金をむしり取る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 善良な経営者の弱みに___、友人を欺くことまで強要して金をむしり取る。
prompt.prompt_en: How loan sharks exploit vulnerabilities. Which verb goes with 弱みに?

feedback.correct_en: 弱みにつけこむ 'to prey on someone's weakness' is the fixed collocation for exploiting another's vulnerability.
feedback.incorrect_en: ぶつかる means 'to collide/clash,' and さわる means 'to touch' — neither fits exploitation.

contrast_examples.jp: 人の弱みにつけこむのは卑怯だ。
contrast_examples.en: Preying on someone's weakness is cowardly.

contrast_examples.jp: 相手の隙を突く。
contrast_examples.en: Exploit an opponent's opening.

prompt.context_jp: ようやく___が下りたせいか、皆の表情は穏やかだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ようやく___が下りたせいか、皆の表情は穏やかだった。
prompt.prompt_en: The ordeal is over and everyone can relax. Which idiom fits?

feedback.correct_en: 肩の荷が下りる 'the load falls off one's shoulders' is the fixed idiom for feeling finally relieved of a burden.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手の荷 and 心の荷 aren't established idioms in Japanese for this meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: 試験が終わって肩の荷が下りた。
contrast_examples.en: With the exam over, a weight lifted off my shoulders.

contrast_examples.jp: 重荷を下ろす。
contrast_examples.en: To put down a heavy burden.

prompt.context_jp: Souma is angry Mai followed him and firmly tells her this isn't her concern.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural as Souma's blunt rebuke in this scene?

choices.text: 何しに来た？ これは俺の問題だって言っただろう
何のために来ましたか？ これは私の問題だと言いましたよね

feedback.correct_en: A is terse, masculine, and matches Souma's irritated boss-to-subordinate register. Short questions + plain だろう fit the sharp pushback.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is over-polite ます/です with 私, which would make Souma sound distant and formal — wrong for scolding his own subordinate in anger.

contrast_examples.jp: 何しに来た？
contrast_examples.en: What did you come for? (blunt)

contrast_examples.jp: どうしていらっしゃったんですか？
contrast_examples.en: What brings you here? (polite)

prompt.context_jp: Souma declares the bank's purpose: to support friends in trouble.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural as the climactic line?

choices.text: こういうときに力になるのが 銀行の役目だ
こういうときに銀行の役目が 力になることだ

feedback.correct_en: A uses the 〜のが Xだ cleft to highlight 'being there in times like this' as the defining role — a punchy, idiomatic frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: B inverts subject and complement awkwardly; '銀行の役目が…ことだ' sounds twisted and loses the emphatic focus.

contrast_examples.jp: 困った人を助けるのが仕事だ。
contrast_examples.en: Helping people in need is the job.

contrast_examples.jp: 仕事が困った人を助けることだ。
contrast_examples.en: (awkward: 'The job is helping people' — stilted order)

prompt.context_jp: Mai, next to Souma in his darkest hour, cannot help him.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing conveys her self-reproach more naturally?

choices.text: 相馬のそばにいながら、自分は何ひとつできなかった
相馬のそばにいながら、自分が何ひとつできなかった

feedback.correct_en: A uses contrastive は on 自分: 'close though I was, as for ME I couldn't do a thing' — the natural self-blame tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's 自分が neutrally identifies the subject, which sounds like a factual report rather than inner regret, and clashes with the 〜ながら contrast.

contrast_examples.jp: そばにいたのに、私は何もできなかった。
contrast_examples.en: I was right there, yet I couldn't do anything. (regret)

contrast_examples.jp: ちょうど私がそばにいた。
contrast_examples.en: I happened to be nearby. (plain fact)

prompt.context_jp: Souma formally apologizes and takes full responsibility to the headquarters.
prompt.prompt_en: Which pair of lines sounds more natural as a formal corporate apology?

choices.text: この度は 誠に 申し訳ありませんでした。責任の所在は 全て私にあります
今回 本当にごめんなさい。責任は全部 僕にあるんです

feedback.correct_en: A uses this chapter's formal register: この度は, 誠に, 申し訳ありませんでした, and the fixed phrase 責任の所在 — the standard script for business apology.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's ごめんなさい/僕/〜んです is personal-casual register, unfit for addressing headquarters about a serious incident.

contrast_examples.jp: この度は、ご迷惑をおかけし誠に申し訳ございません。
contrast_examples.en: We sincerely apologize for the trouble on this occasion.

contrast_examples.jp: ごめんね、迷惑かけちゃって。
contrast_examples.en: Sorry for bothering you. (casual)

prompt.context_jp: Souma places his hand on Aoi's shoulder and gives him hope.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural as Souma's quiet, resolute reply?

choices.text: まだ終わりではないのです

feedback.correct_en: A is the plain, short line that lands with emotional weight between two old friends — matches Souma's quiet resolve.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's のです makes it sound like an explanation to a stranger or in a speech, breaking the intimate friend-to-friend moment.

contrast_examples.jp: まだ終わりじゃない。
contrast_examples.en: It's not over yet. (close, firm)

contrast_examples.jp: まだ終わってはおりません。
contrast_examples.en: It has not yet ended. (very formal)
